result.summary: I've asked the landlord to decide how to proceed with the bedroom radiator, and nothing has been booked. Their approval (event 3) only covered Harlow Heating, up to £150. Harlow can't come until 3 November unless it's an emergency visit at double rate (event 4). The other offer, from Quick Fix, is £230, which is over the cap and a different contractor (event 5). I've emailed the landlord the three options, updated the tenant and asked whether anyone in the household is vulnerable, and put the case on hold to follow up in one day.
result.situation: At 27 Thistle Lane, one bedroom radiator isn't heating; the rest of the house is fine. The landlord approved the repair only with Harlow Heating and up to £150. Harlow is fully booked until 3 November (sooner only as an emergency visit at double rate). Quick Fix Heating can attend Monday 6 October and quotes £230 including parts.

judgement.why_this_decision: The landlord's approval in event 3 explicitly excludes other contractors and anything over £150 without asking first. Both options available now break those conditions: Quick Fix at £230 (event 5) and a Harlow emergency visit at double rate (event 4). Only the landlord can make this decision, and they can answer quickly, so I asked them directly rather than escalating. One cold room with the rest of the house heated, and no known vulnerability, doesn't meet the emergency criteria, so this doesn't justify acting without approval.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The landlord limited the job to Harlow Heating and £150; booking Quick Fix would breach both conditions.
It is double rate with no price given, and would likely go over the £150 cap.

alternatives_considered.option: Wait for Harlow on 3 November without asking
alternatives_considered.why_not: That would leave the tenant's bedroom without heating for a month without giving the landlord the choice.
The landlord can resolve this themselves; I'll escalate if they don't reply or if the tenant turns out to be vulnerable.
Only one room is affected, the rest of the house is heated, and no vulnerability is recorded. I've asked the tenant about vulnerability.
